title: JB Hi-Fi Limited - Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee of any JB Hi-Fi Group company, including each Key Person. Only Sections 1 and 2 (the insider trading prohibition) apply to Employees who are not Key Persons; the trading windows, approval, hedging and margin lending rules in Section 3 do not.

tiers.name: Key Persons
tiers.description: KMP of the JB Hi-Fi Group within AASB 124 plus certain other key employees: any Director, the Group Executive team, the Executive teams of the JB Hi-Fi, The Good Guys and E&S businesses, members of the senior management teams, area and territory managers, Support Office employees in Australia and New Zealand, store managers, store office administrators and administrators, and anyone else designated by the Company Secretary. All Sections of the Policy apply to Key Persons: trading windows, the 6 month rule and the unvested hedging ban. Only the sub-group listed in section 3.8 (Directors, Group and business Executive teams, Company Secretary, direct reports of the Group CFO, the legal team and any person designated by the Company Secretary) needs prior written approval to Deal inside a Trading Window.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A director of JB Hi-Fi Limited, executive or non-executive. Additional obligations: prior approval from the Chairman for all Dealing, the short selling ban, the margin lending approval and 24 hour disclosure regime, the economic-risk-altering approval regime in section 3.32, and notification of Dealings to the Company Secretary within 24 hours.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Group level executives and executives of the JB Hi-Fi, The Good Guys and E&S businesses. Subject to the same short selling ban, margin lending approval and disclosure regime, and section 3.32 approval regime for hedging vested holdings, as Directors; approval comes from the Chairman for Group Executives and the Company Secretary or Group CEO for business Executives.

definitions.hedging_definition: any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant ... irrespective of the outcome under that incentive award or grant

windows.start_anchor: the day following lodgement of the Company's half year profit announcement with the ASX
the day following lodgement of the Company's annual profit announcement with the ASX
the day after the Company's annual general meeting
all other times outside the three Trading Windows
windows.end_anchor: the start of the next Trading Window

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time restrict Dealing during any Trading Window by all or particular Key Persons or other Employees by notice to them (a 'Prohibited Period'), for example where they are aware of price sensitive facts. The restriction is confidential and must not be disclosed. The Company may also extend the Policy to Securities of other specified companies with which it deals.

rules.detail: A put and call collar over vested JB Hi-Fi Securities is expressly contemplated: 'collars' are named in the Derivatives definition and section 3.32 requires prior written approval of the Chairman on the Approval Request Form before entering any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging and other derivative products) that alters economic benefit or risk in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities not caught by the unvested ban. There is no venue limit, so an OTC structure with a bank is covered. Post-trade notification to the Company Secretary is required and the Company may disclose it publicly.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities (whether received under an equity-based incentive award scheme or otherwise) which are not subject to the prohibition in section 3.30 above.

rules.detail: Same regime as Directors: prior written approval on the Approval Request Form, approval valid 5 trading days, revocable, plus prompt post-trade notification to the Company Secretary. Approver is the Chairman for Group Executives and the Company Secretary or Group CEO for business Executives.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities

rules.detail: For Key Persons who are not Directors or Executives, section 3.32 does not apply, but entry into a Derivative in relation to Securities is a Dealing, so it must occur in a Trading Window and outside any Prohibited Period. Only the section 3.8 sub-group (Directors, Group and business Executive teams, Company Secretary, Group CFO direct reports, legal team and designated persons) needs prior written approval within a window; other Key Persons do not.
rules.evidence: Deal or Dealing includes, in relation to Securities, an acquisition or disposal of Securities, or entry into a Derivative in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any derivative that alters the economic benefit or risk of an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant. Applies to every Key Person including Directors and Executives.
rules.evidence: No Key Person may enter into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant made by the Company to the Key Person, irrespective of the outcome under that incentive award or grant.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements over unvested equity incentive awards are prohibited outright for all Key Persons; there is no exemption or approval mechanism for this prohibition.
rules.evidence: No Key Person may enter into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant

rules.detail: Hedging of vested holdings, whether acquired under an incentive scheme or bought on market, is permitted with prior written approval of the Chairman; the decision is wholly discretionary, final and binding, revocable before Dealing, and any refusal is confidential. Approval lasts 5 trading days. Notification to the Company Secretary as soon as reasonably practicable after entry, and the Company may publish the arrangement.
rules.evidence: In addition, any Director or Executive taking such action must notify the Company Secretary as soon as reasonably practicable after any such scheme, arrangement or agreement is entered into. JB Hi-Fi may publicly disclose this information irrespective of whether it is technically required by law or the ASX Listing Rules.

rules.detail: Identical regime to Directors: discretionary prior written approval of the Relevant Company Officer, 5 trading day validity, revocable, followed by prompt notification and possible public disclosure.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement (including options, hedging arrangements and other derivative products) under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities

rules.detail: For Key Persons who are not Directors or Executives, the unvested hedging ban falls away on vesting and exercisability, and section 3.32 approval does not apply to them; the hedge remains a Dealing subject to Trading Windows, Prohibited Periods, the 6 month rule and (for the section 3.8 sub-group) prior written approval.
rules.evidence: Once any equity-based incentive award or grant made by JB Hi-Fi to a Key Person (who is not a Director or Executive) is vested and is exercisable, the restriction in section 3.30 above does not apply. However, any actions in respect of such awards or grants are subject to the restrictions on Dealing in Securities set out in this Policy.

rules.detail: The section 3.30 ban is lifted only once an award is both vested and exercisable, so awards that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or are not yet exercisable stay within the absolute prohibition on altering economic benefit or risk.
rules.evidence: Once any equity-based incentive award or grant made by JB Hi-Fi to a Key Person (who is not a Director or Executive) is vested and is exercisable, the restriction in section 3.30 above does not apply.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named as such, but a prepaid forward, zero-cost collar with funding or similar structure alters the economic benefit or risk derived from JB Hi-Fi Securities and is an entry into a Derivative and an agreement to dispose, so it requires section 3.32 approval, must be within a Trading Window unless separately approved, and must be notified afterwards.
rules.evidence: Derivatives includes derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars) and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.

rules.detail: Not named for Key Persons generally. A monetisation is an entry into a Derivative, an agreement to dispose, or a transaction involving a change in beneficial interest, and so is a Dealing that must occur in a Trading Window and, for the section 3.8 sub-group, with prior written approval.
rules.evidence: or the engagement in any other transaction involving a beneficial interest or a change in the beneficial ownership of the Securities, or the entry into any agreement to do any of the above things.

rules.detail: Absolute ban that overrides the Trading Windows; there is no approval route.
rules.evidence: For this reason, Directors and Executives are prohibited from short selling JB Hi-Fi Securities, even during Trading Windows.

rules.detail: Same absolute ban as for Directors, applying even during Trading Windows.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are prohibited from short selling JB Hi-Fi Securities, even during Trading Windows.

rules.detail: The express prohibition in section 3.29 is directed only at Directors and Executives. For other Key Persons a short sale is a disposal of Securities and so a Dealing confined to Trading Windows and, for the section 3.8 sub-group, subject to prior approval; it would also normally breach the 6 month rule.
rules.evidence: Short selling involves a person borrowing a security (e.g. JB Hi-Fi Securities) and selling it in the hope that they will be able to buy back the security at a lower price at some point in the future

rules.detail: Securities lending by a holder is nowhere addressed; borrowing appears only in the description of short selling in section 3.27, and lending is not listed in the definition of Deal.

CFDs are not named, but they are derivatives within section 761D and alter the economic benefit or risk derived from JB Hi-Fi Securities, so section 3.32 approval applies; a short CFD would in substance breach the section 3.29 short selling ban and the 6 month rule.
rules.evidence: Derivatives includes derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: Not named. A CFD over JB Hi-Fi Securities is entry into a Derivative in relation to Securities, hence a Dealing confined to Trading Windows, and its short-term nature would normally offend the 6 month rule.
rules.evidence: Deal or Dealing includes, in relation to Securities, ... entry into a Derivative in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted, not banned, but requires prior written approval of the Chairman on the Approval Request Form (valid 5 trading days, revocable, refusal confidential), written disclosure to the Company Secretary within 24 hours of entry, periodic reporting to the Board and possible voluntary public disclosure.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives may not include their JB Hi-Fi Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement or otherwise Deal in their JB Hi-Fi Securities pursuant to a margin lending or similar funding arrangement, without first obtaining the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer using the Approval Request Form

rules.detail: Identical regime to Directors, with approval from the Chairman for Group Executives and the Company Secretary or Group CEO for business Executives, plus the 24 hour written disclosure to the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: any margin lending or similar funding arrangements entered into by any Director or Executive in relation to JB Hi-Fi Securities must be disclosed in writing to the Company Secretary as soon as practicable after entry into such an arrangement and, in any case, not more than 24 hours afterwards.

rules.detail: Section 3.22 is expressed to apply only to Directors and Executives. For other Key Persons, putting Securities into a margin loan is a use of the Securities as security and so a Dealing subject to Trading Windows and, for the section 3.8 sub-group, prior approval.
rules.evidence: or the use of the Securities as security or the grant of any encumbrance over the Securities

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge or other security interest over JB Hi-Fi Securities is expressly within the definition of Dealing, so it must be done in a Trading Window and, for the section 3.8 sub-group, with prior written approval. There is no outright prohibition on encumbering shares.
rules.evidence: or the use of the Securities as security or the grant of any encumbrance over the Securities

rules.detail: For a Director, granting security over JB Hi-Fi Securities to a lender is both a Dealing (use as security) and, where it is part of a margin lending or similar funding arrangement, subject to the express section 3.22 approval and 24 hour disclosure regime. Approval comes from the Chairman.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives may not include their JB Hi-Fi Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement or otherwise Deal in their JB Hi-Fi Securities pursuant to a margin lending or similar funding arrangement, without first obtaining the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer

rules.detail: The policy covers not only margin loans but any 'similar funding arrangement' secured on JB Hi-Fi Securities, including a bank loan secured against collared shares. It is permitted subject to discretionary prior written approval of the Chairman, disclosure to the Company Secretary within 24 hours, periodic Board reporting and possible voluntary public disclosure. No prohibition and no security-state limitation, although shares under an unvested award could not be pledged without breaching section 3.30 only if the pledge altered economic risk.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives may not include their JB Hi-Fi Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement or otherwise Deal in their JB Hi-Fi Securities pursuant to a margin lending or similar funding arrangement, without first obtaining the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer

rules.detail: Same regime as Directors: approval by the Relevant Company Officer, 24 hour written disclosure of the arrangement to the Company Secretary, periodic reporting to the Board and possible public disclosure by the Company.
rules.evidence: JB Hi-Fi may also publicly disclose any margin loan or similar funding arrangements over JB Hi-Fi Securities taken out by any Director or Executive irrespective of whether such disclosure is required by law or the ASX Listing Rules.

rules.detail: A Key Person may not Deal in the same JB Hi-Fi Securities within any 6 month period. Carve-out for the acquisition, vesting or exercise of options under a JB Hi-Fi Option Plan and the subsequent sale of the resulting Securities within 6 months. As entry into a Derivative is a Dealing, a collar and its unwind or roll within 6 months over the same Securities is exposed to this restriction.
rules.evidence: Key Persons are encouraged to be long-term holders of JB Hi-Fi Securities and may not therefore Deal in the same JB Hi-Fi Securities within any 6 month period.

exemption_authority: The Relevant Company Officer (Chairman for Directors, Group Executives and the Company Secretary; chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman; Company Secretary or Group CEO for other Key Persons) may approve Dealing inside a Closed Period or Prohibited Period on the Approval Request Form, likely only for severe financial hardship, transfers to connected persons, where all price relevant information has recently been disclosed, or other exceptional circumstances such as a legal or court order requirement. The decision is entirely discretionary, needs no reasons, is final and binding, and evidence of the claimed circumstances may be demanded.

bespoke_clauses.topic: collars named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives includes derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars) and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is expressly within scope, so both legs are Dealings and the substance test catches any economically equivalent structure, but nothing prohibits a collar over vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives must obtain the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer ... before entering into any scheme, arrangement or agreement ... under which the relevant Director or Executive may alter the economic benefit or risk they derive in relation to any JB Hi-Fi Securities (whether received under an equity-based incentive award scheme or otherwise).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar is available to Directors and Executives over vested and on-market shares but only on a wholly discretionary approval that may be refused without reasons and revoked before execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: voluntary public disclosure of hedges and loans
bespoke_clauses.clause: JB Hi-Fi may publicly disclose this information irrespective of whether it is technically required by law or the ASX Listing Rules.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the collar and the secured loan may be announced to the market even where no legal disclosure obligation exists, so the client cannot rely on confidentiality.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives may not include their JB Hi-Fi Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement ... without first obtaining the written approval of the Relevant Company Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted subject to approval and disclosure rather than prohibited, so a funded structure is achievable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval given under section 3.22 by the Relevant Company Officer will be valid for a period of 5 trading days, commencing on the date it is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of both the collar and the loan must complete within 5 trading days of each approval or fresh approval is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval given may be revoked in writing (including by email) by the Relevant Company Officer prior to Dealing taking place if new information comes to light, or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank faces execution risk that a signed but unsettled collar or drawdown is withdrawn at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Persons ... may not therefore Deal in the same JB Hi-Fi Securities within any 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor, rolls, partial unwinds and any sale of the collared parcel should be spaced at least six months apart, since each is a Dealing in the same Securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any restriction on Dealing in JB Hi-Fi Securities during a Trading Window which is notified by the Company to all or particular Key Persons or other Employees is a confidential matter which must not be disclosed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The client may be unable to tell the bank why a scheduled entry, roll or physical settlement cannot proceed, so the documentation must tolerate silent postponement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Key Person may enter into any scheme, arrangement or agreement ... under which the relevant Key Person may alter the economic benefit or risk derived by the Key Person, in relation to an unvested equity-based incentive award or grant.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only vested and exercisable holdings can be collared; the bank must verify vesting and exercisability before sizing the trade, as there is no approval route for unvested awards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees should ensure that any Securities trading which is prohibited by this Policy is not undertaken by: their spouse, partner or child; ... a company or trust over which the Employee has influence or control (regardless of who is the beneficiary) including any self managed superannuation fund.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or loan through a family trust, SMSF or controlled company does not avoid the approval and disclosure requirements.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no relief for shares under option plans
bespoke_clauses.clause: This may prevent, for example, Key Persons selling, and realising the value of, shares resulting from the exercise of options under a JB Hi-Fi Option Plan at a particular time, even though the Plan rules would otherwise allow this.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement of the collar out of plan shares can be blocked by a Prohibited Period notwithstanding the plan rules, so cash settlement or a delivery grace period should be provided for.

summary: A funded collar is achievable for a JB Hi-Fi Director or Executive over vested and exercisable shares, but only with two discretionary approvals and prompt disclosure. The derivative legs require prior written approval of the Relevant Company Officer under section 3.32 because a collar alters the economic benefit or risk derived from JB Hi-Fi Securities (collars are named in the Derivatives definition), and the loan secured on the collared shares requires separate approval under section 3.22 as a 'margin lending or similar funding arrangement'; each approval is valid for 5 trading days, may be refused without reasons and may be revoked before execution. The arrangement must be entered into during one of the three 4 week Trading Windows unless closed-period approval is obtained, must not involve unvested awards (section 3.30 bans hedging these outright, with no exemption), and must not conflict with the ban on Key Persons Dealing in the same Securities within any 6 month period. Both the loan and the hedge must be reported to the Company Secretary (within 24 hours for financing arrangements), are reported periodically to the Board and may be publicly disclosed by JB Hi-Fi even where no law requires it. The policy is silent on forced sales and margin calls, so the documentation should address what happens if enforcement or physical settlement falls in a Closed or confidential Prohibited Period.
